analysis:
I found no concrete security regression in the supplied units.

.github/workflows/ci.yml (head text only, lines 1-778; no patch was supplied, so I could not tell which lines changed). The visible content is CI test orchestration. Third-party actions are pinned by SHA, except two cache actions: lines 373/384 pin a SHA without a version comment, and lines 683/729/750 pin a SHA with a comment. No secrets, deploy steps, or pull_request_target usage appear. Concurrency (lines 9-11) cancels only same-PR runs. The `changes` job sets `contents: read` (lines 16-17); other jobs inherit the repository default token permissions, which this excerpt cannot show. The gate job (lines 691-713) requires selected provider lanes to be success, or skipped when no provider change was detected. Line 43 adds `test-app-attest-entitlements.py` to the release-integrity checks, and line 288 adds `test-profile-inventory-auth.py`. Both support the TB-011 and MDM-removal terminal-auth assumptions in the canonical context. Lines 358-359 and 368-369 set DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 only for specific isolated native test steps (T-041 kill switch, test scope only). That is test-only and does not change the production default-on posture.

CHANGELOG.md: documentation only. It describes a provider drain/retire retry for native MiMo owners after served requests, and a `Not serving:` line in `darkbloom status`. The provider source for these changes was not supplied. A reviewer should confirm that the retried retirement stays within the drain deadline and does not re-enable serving authorization (T-053, T-057), and that the status output exposes no identifiers (T-058).

Coverage limit: no provider or coordinator source and no CI patch was supplied, so the stated behavior changes could not be verified.
